flawed_step: Step 2: Inferring that the two stratum-wise inequalities imply the overall inequality. The overall rates use different weights, P(C|T) and P(C|not-T), so the inequalities cannot be combined as though both sides had the same mixture weights.
counterexample: Take 100 treated and 100 untreated individuals. Among treated: in C, 9/10 succeed; in not-C, 18/90 succeed. Among untreated: in C, 72/90 succeed; in not-C, 1/10 succeeds. Thus 9/10>72/90 and 18/90>1/10 within the strata, but overall 27/100<73/100.
assessment_summary: Step 1, expanding each overall rate by conditioning on C, is justified. The proof stops at Step 2 because the stratum weights differ between treatment groups. Indeed, the displayed finite example satisfies all positivity assumptions and reverses the claimed overall inequality (Simpson's paradox).
